questions.stem: This illustration depicts a heart with the outer sac being stripped away, shown in a normal state and after removal. For which condition is the procedure being illustrated the definitive surgical treatment?

explanation.summary: The image shows pericardiectomy, surgical removal of the fibrotic, non-compliant pericardium. It is the definitive treatment for markedly symptomatic constrictive pericarditis, relieving the external constraint on ventricular filling, though operative mortality is relatively high.
explanation.whyCorrect: The image shows pericardiectomy, surgical removal of the fibrotic, non-compliant pericardium. It is the definitive treatment for markedly symptomatic constrictive pericarditis, relieving the external constraint on ventricular filling, though operative mortality is relatively high.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the layered anatomy of the pericardium. Excess fluid accumulating in the space between the visceral and parietal pericardium, compressing the heart, defines which condition?

explanation.summary: The space labeled between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal pericardium is the pericardial cavity. When fluid there accumulates rapidly or in large volume it compresses the chambers and impairs filling, producing cardiac tamponade, a life-threatening cause of obstructive shock.
explanation.whyCorrect: The space labeled between the visceral (epicardial) and parietal pericardium is the pericardial cavity. When fluid there accumulates rapidly or in large volume it compresses the chambers and impairs filling, producing cardiac tamponade, a life-threatening cause of obstructive shock.

questions.stem: This anterior view of the great vessels shows the aortic arch and its branches. Based on the branching pattern illustrated, how do the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries arise relative to the arch?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They share a common left brachiocephalic trunk

choices.label: B
choices.text: They both branch from a single brachiocephalic trunk with the carotids

choices.label: C
choices.text: They branch from the pulmonary trunk

choices.label: D
choices.text: They arise from the descending thoracic aorta

choices.label: E
choices.text: They arise separately and independently from the arch

explanation.summary: On the left, the common carotid and subclavian arteries arise separately and directly from the aortic arch, unlike the right side where a brachiocephalic trunk first divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. This asymmetry reflects the differing embryologic remodeling of the aortic arches.
explanation.whyCorrect: On the left, the common carotid and subclavian arteries arise separately and directly from the aortic arch, unlike the right side where a brachiocephalic trunk first divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. This asymmetry reflects the differing embryologic remodeling of the aortic arches.

questions.stem: This lateral view of an early embryo shows a series of ridges labeled as pharyngeal arches. The major arteries and connective/muscular structures derived from these arches ultimately supply which body region?

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lower back and vertebral column

explanation.summary: The pharyngeal (branchial) arches shown remodel to form the great arteries and other structures of the head, neck, and thorax. Somites, the heart bulge, lens placode, and otic placode are also visible, marking key landmarks of the developing embryo.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pharyngeal (branchial) arches shown remodel to form the great arteries and other structures of the head, neck, and thorax. Somites, the heart bulge, lens placode, and otic placode are also visible, marking key landmarks of the developing embryo.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal aortic arch (left) with a congenital abnormality of the arch (right). In this defect, where is the narrowing most commonly located?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the bifurcation of the aorta into the common iliac arteries

choices.label: B
choices.text: At the aortic root within the sinuses of Valsalva

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the abdominal aorta at the level of the renal arteries

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the ascending aorta just above the aortic valve

choices.label: E
choices.text: In the descending aorta, just distal to the left subclavian artery near the ligamentum arteriosum

explanation.summary: Coarctation of the aorta is a stricture of the aortic lumen most often located in the descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery, near the attachment of the ligamentum arteriosum (the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus).
explanation.whyCorrect: Coarctation of the aorta is a stricture of the aortic lumen most often located in the descending aorta just distal to the left subclavian artery, near the attachment of the ligamentum arteriosum (the remnant of the fetal ductus arteriosus).

questions.stem: The valve illustrated on the right has one fewer cusp than the normal valve on the left. This congenital variant most strongly predisposes the patient to which condition?

explanation.summary: The valve on the right is a bicuspid aortic valve (two cusps instead of three). Abnormal leaflet mechanics accelerate calcification, so these patients typically develop aortic stenosis decades earlier than those with a normal tricuspid valve.
explanation.whyCorrect: The valve on the right is a bicuspid aortic valve (two cusps instead of three). Abnormal leaflet mechanics accelerate calcification, so these patients typically develop aortic stenosis decades earlier than those with a normal tricuspid valve.

questions.stem: The right-hand cross-sectional view of this specimen is taken through the plane of all four cardiac valves. Which structure does this cross-section best demonstrate as the common anchor for the valves?

explanation.summary: A short-axis section at the level of the valves shows the dense fibrous cardiac skeleton, a ring of connective tissue that surrounds and anchors all four valve annuli and electrically insulates the atria from the ventricles.
explanation.whyCorrect: A short-axis section at the level of the valves shows the dense fibrous cardiac skeleton, a ring of connective tissue that surrounds and anchors all four valve annuli and electrically insulates the atria from the ventricles.

questions.stem: The schematic on the left illustrates the anatomic variant of aortic dissection that involves the ascending aorta. Compared with the variant on the right, what is the standard initial management of the type shown on the left?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Balloon angioplasty of the aortic arch

explanation.summary: The left diagram is a Stanford type A dissection (involving the ascending aorta), which is more dangerous and requires immediate surgical intervention. The right (type B) dissection, which spares the ascending aorta, is generally managed medically.
explanation.whyCorrect: The left diagram is a Stanford type A dissection (involving the ascending aorta), which is more dangerous and requires immediate surgical intervention. The right (type B) dissection, which spares the ascending aorta, is generally managed medically.

questions.stem: This diagram of the head and neck arterial tree illustrates the vessels relevant to the most feared complication of giant cell arteritis. Which complication does occlusion within this arterial supply produce?

explanation.summary: In GCA, ischemia from vasculitis occludes the posterior ciliary branches of the ophthalmic artery (which arises from the internal carotid), causing anterior ischemic optic neuropathy and irreversible blindness. This is why steroids are started before biopsy results return.
explanation.whyCorrect: In GCA, ischemia from vasculitis occludes the posterior ciliary branches of the ophthalmic artery (which arises from the internal carotid), causing anterior ischemic optic neuropathy and irreversible blindness. This is why steroids are started before biopsy results return.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the arteries arising from the aortic root and running in the grooves of the heart. Sudden thrombotic occlusion of the vessel descending in the anterior interventricular groove would most directly compromise perfusion of which region?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Posterior wall of the left atrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: Right atrium and SA node region

choices.label: C
choices.text: Inferior (diaphragmatic) wall of the left ventricle

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lateral free wall of the right ventricle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anterior wall and interventricular septum of the left ventricle

explanation.summary: The vessel shown running down the anterior interventricular groove is the left anterior descending (LAD) artery, a branch of the left main coronary artery. It supplies the anterior LV wall and most of the interventricular septum, so its occlusion produces an anterior/anteroseptal infarct.
explanation.whyCorrect: The vessel shown running down the anterior interventricular groove is the left anterior descending (LAD) artery, a branch of the left main coronary artery. It supplies the anterior LV wall and most of the interventricular septum, so its occlusion produces an anterior/anteroseptal infarct.

questions.stem: This surgical illustration depicts an open operation at the carotid bifurcation in which the artery is incised and the diseased intimal plaque is dissected free and removed, restoring the lumen. What is this procedure called?

explanation.summary: Endarterectomy removes the atheromatous plaque and inner arterial layer through an open arteriotomy, directly relieving high-grade stenosis in symptomatic patients.
explanation.whyCorrect: Endarterectomy removes the atheromatous plaque and inner arterial layer through an open arteriotomy, directly relieving high-grade stenosis in symptomatic patients.

questions.stem: This diagram of the coronary circulation labels the major epicardial vessels arising from the aorta. Which labeled artery principally supplies the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle?

choices.label: C
choices.text: The left anterior descending coronary artery

explanation.summary: In most hearts the right coronary artery supplies the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle as well as the right ventricle, which is why inferior infarcts are typically attributed to RCA occlusion. The LAD supplies the anterior wall and the circumflex the lateral wall.
explanation.whyCorrect: In most hearts the right coronary artery supplies the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle as well as the right ventricle, which is why inferior infarcts are typically attributed to RCA occlusion. The LAD supplies the anterior wall and the circumflex the lateral wall.

questions.stem: The dilated, tortuous vessels seen bulging beneath the skin of this patient's leg belong to which part of the venous system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The deep venous system beneath the muscular fascia

choices.label: B
choices.text: The perforating arteries of the calf

choices.label: E
choices.text: The muscular venous sinusoids of the soleus

explanation.summary: Varicose veins are dilated, tortuous veins of the superficial venous system, which lies above the deep fascia. Valvular incompetence in these superficial veins causes them to become engorged and visibly tortuous.
explanation.whyCorrect: Varicose veins are dilated, tortuous veins of the superficial venous system, which lies above the deep fascia. Valvular incompetence in these superficial veins causes them to become engorged and visibly tortuous.

questions.stem: This cross-sectional diagram shows a side view of the mitral valve apparatus, including its leaflets, chordae, and papillary muscles. If the papillary muscles or the cords they anchor fail to hold the leaflets closed during ventricular systole, which valvular disorder results?

explanation.summary: The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles keep the leaflets from flipping back into the left atrium during systole; loss of that competence allows systolic backflow, i.e. mitral regurgitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles keep the leaflets from flipping back into the left atrium during systole; loss of that competence allows systolic backflow, i.e. mitral regurgitation.

questions.stem: This composite figure compares normal mitral valve anatomy with surgical views showing placement of a prosthetic ring around the valve annulus and a prosthetic valve. This type of intervention is most often performed to treat which condition?

explanation.summary: Annuloplasty ring repair or prosthetic valve replacement restores leaflet coaptation and is the definitive treatment for symptomatic severe mitral regurgitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Annuloplasty ring repair or prosthetic valve replacement restores leaflet coaptation and is the definitive treatment for symptomatic severe mitral regurgitation.

questions.stem: In this posterior external view of the heart, the vessels highlighted in yellow entering the upper chamber are the single most common anatomical source of the ectopic electrical triggers that initiate a specific supraventricular arrhythmia. Which arrhythmia is that?

explanation.summary: The yellow-highlighted vessels are the pulmonary veins draining into the left atrium. Ectopic foci at the pulmonary vein ostia are the most common trigger for atrial fibrillation, which is why pulmonary vein isolation is the cornerstone of AF ablation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The yellow-highlighted vessels are the pulmonary veins draining into the left atrium. Ectopic foci at the pulmonary vein ostia are the most common trigger for atrial fibrillation, which is why pulmonary vein isolation is the cornerstone of AF ablation.

questions.stem: This schematic shows a subcutaneous pulse generator connected by leads that pass through the right heart chambers, with specialized coil segments on the leads capable of delivering a shock. What device is depicted?

explanation.summary: A pulse generator with pacing/sensing leads plus dedicated shock coils able to detect and terminate ventricular tachyarrhythmias represents an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, which combines pacing capability with high-energy defibrillation.
explanation.whyCorrect: A pulse generator with pacing/sensing leads plus dedicated shock coils able to detect and terminate ventricular tachyarrhythmias represents an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator, which combines pacing capability with high-energy defibrillation.

questions.stem: The right-hand cross-section shows all four cardiac valves lying in a single plane embedded within a ring of dense connective tissue. What is the principal functional role of this fibrous structure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It stores calcium to trigger myocardial relaxation

choices.label: B
choices.text: It electrically insulates the atria from the ventricles so conduction is forced through the AV node

choices.label: C
choices.text: It actively contracts to eject blood from the ventricles

choices.label: D
choices.text: It generates the pacemaker impulse that initiates each heartbeat

choices.label: E
choices.text: It supplies oxygenated blood to the valve leaflets

explanation.summary: The valves sit in the fibrous cardiac skeleton, which anchors the leaflets and myocardium and electrically insulates the atria from the ventricles, restricting the only conduction pathway to the AV node. This is why the tricuspid and mitral valves are shown closed during diastole in the same plane.
explanation.whyCorrect: The valves sit in the fibrous cardiac skeleton, which anchors the leaflets and myocardium and electrically insulates the atria from the ventricles, restricting the only conduction pathway to the AV node. This is why the tricuspid and mitral valves are shown closed during diastole in the same plane.

questions.stem: This side view shows the valve situated between the left atrium and left ventricle. How many leaflets does this valve normally have?

explanation.summary: The mitral (bicuspid) valve has two leaflets, an anterior and a posterior leaflet, anchored by chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles. This distinguishes it from the tricuspid, aortic, and pulmonic valves, which each have three cusps.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mitral (bicuspid) valve has two leaflets, an anterior and a posterior leaflet, anchored by chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles. This distinguishes it from the tricuspid, aortic, and pulmonic valves, which each have three cusps.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the mitral valve with its leaflets connected by thin cords to the papillary muscles. Sudden rupture of these cords would most likely produce which acute condition?

explanation.summary: The chordae tendineae anchor the leaflets to the papillary muscles and hold the valve closed during systole. Loss of this tethering lets a leaflet flail into the left atrium, causing acute mitral regurgitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The chordae tendineae anchor the leaflets to the papillary muscles and hold the valve closed during systole. Loss of this tethering lets a leaflet flail into the left atrium, causing acute mitral regurgitation.

questions.stem: These operative views show a prosthetic ring being seated around the dilated mitral annulus to restore leaflet coaptation. What is this valve-sparing surgical procedure called?

explanation.summary: Placing a ring to remodel and reduce the annular circumference (annuloplasty) restores coaptation and is a mainstay of mitral valve repair, preserving the native leaflets rather than replacing the valve.
explanation.whyCorrect: Placing a ring to remodel and reduce the annular circumference (annuloplasty) restores coaptation and is a mainstay of mitral valve repair, preserving the native leaflets rather than replacing the valve.

questions.stem: This gross cadaveric dissection views a right-sided atrioventricular valve from above, with its three leaflets labeled Anterior, Septal, and Inferior and the surrounding coronary arteries and AV node artery identified. Which valve is being displayed?

explanation.summary: A three-leaflet (anterior, septal, inferior/posterior) atrioventricular valve seated between the right atrium and right ventricle, adjacent to the AV node artery and right coronary artery, is the tricuspid valve. The mitral valve has only two leaflets, and the aortic and pulmonary valves are semilunar valves with three cusps but no chordae/leaflet arrangement.
explanation.whyCorrect: A three-leaflet (anterior, septal, inferior/posterior) atrioventricular valve seated between the right atrium and right ventricle, adjacent to the AV node artery and right coronary artery, is the tricuspid valve. The mitral valve has only two leaflets, and the aortic and pulmonary valves are semilunar valves with three cusps but no chordae/leaflet arrangement.

questions.stem: This side-view schematic shows an atrioventricular valve with two leaflets (a small anterior leaflet and a larger three-lobed posterior leaflet) anchored by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles within the ventricle. Which valve is depicted?

explanation.summary: A bileaflet atrioventricular valve with a scalloped three-lobed posterior leaflet tethered by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles is the mitral valve, which separates the left atrium from the left ventricle. The tricuspid valve has three leaflets, and the aortic and pulmonary valves are semilunar valves lacking chordae and papillary muscles.
explanation.whyCorrect: A bileaflet atrioventricular valve with a scalloped three-lobed posterior leaflet tethered by chordae tendineae to papillary muscles is the mitral valve, which separates the left atrium from the left ventricle. The tricuspid valve has three leaflets, and the aortic and pulmonary valves are semilunar valves lacking chordae and papillary muscles.

questions.stem: This side view of the mitral valve labels its leaflets, chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. During which phase of the cardiac cycle do these leaflets normally open to allow flow?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continuously throughout the entire cardiac cycle

explanation.summary: The mitral valve opens during diastole to permit blood to flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle, and closes during systole to prevent backflow. The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles tether the leaflets to prevent prolapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: The mitral valve opens during diastole to permit blood to flow from the left atrium into the left ventricle, and closes during systole to prevent backflow. The chordae tendineae and papillary muscles tether the leaflets to prevent prolapse.

questions.stem: This labeled illustration shows the layered wall that encloses the heart. In the healthy state, what normally occupies the space between the parietal and visceral serous layers?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A small amount of serous (pericardial) fluid

explanation.summary: The pericardial cavity, located between the parietal and visceral layers of the serous pericardium, normally contains a small amount of serous fluid that reduces friction as the heart contracts and relaxes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pericardial cavity, located between the parietal and visceral layers of the serous pericardium, normally contains a small amount of serous fluid that reduces friction as the heart contracts and relaxes.

questions.stem: This diagram of an early embryo labels a series of pharyngeal (branchial) arches along the head and neck region. The arteries that course through these pharyngeal arches are the embryonic precursors of which group of adult vessels?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The coronary arteries supplying the myocardium

choices.label: B
choices.text: The great arteries and their branches (aortic arch derivatives)

choices.label: C
choices.text: The systemic and cardinal veins that form the vena cavae

choices.label: D
choices.text: The four pulmonary veins draining into the left atrium

choices.label: E
choices.text: The umbilical and vitelline venous system

explanation.summary: The paired arteries of the pharyngeal (aortic) arches remodel into the great arteries: the 3rd arch forms the common carotids, the 4th contributes to the arch of the aorta and proximal right subclavian, and the 6th forms the pulmonary arteries and the ductus arteriosus. The veins, coronary arteries, and pulmonary veins arise from separate developmental fields.
explanation.whyCorrect: The paired arteries of the pharyngeal (aortic) arches remodel into the great arteries: the 3rd arch forms the common carotids, the 4th contributes to the arch of the aorta and proximal right subclavian, and the 6th forms the pulmonary arteries and the ductus arteriosus. The veins, coronary arteries, and pulmonary veins arise from separate developmental fields.

questions.stem: The schematic shows the paired embryonic aortic arches connecting the aortic sac to the dorsal aortae. Which of these arches normally persists to form the definitive arch of the aorta in the adult?

explanation.summary: Of the six paired aortic arches, the left fourth arch persists as the arch of the aorta; the left sixth forms the ductus arteriosus, the third arches contribute to the carotid system, and the first, second, and fifth largely regress.
explanation.whyCorrect: Of the six paired aortic arches, the left fourth arch persists as the arch of the aorta; the left sixth forms the ductus arteriosus, the third arches contribute to the carotid system, and the first, second, and fifth largely regress.

questions.stem: In this dissection view of the great vessels and neck, the right recurrent laryngeal nerve is labeled. Around which structure does this nerve hook on the right side?

explanation.summary: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath and around the right subclavian artery before ascending to the larynx, whereas the left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around the arch of the aorta near the ligamentum arteriosum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The right recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath and around the right subclavian artery before ascending to the larynx, whereas the left recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks around the arch of the aorta near the ligamentum arteriosum.

questions.stem: These schematics classify aortic coarctation by its position relative to the ductus arteriosus. The preductal type shown on the left is most likely the result of abnormal development of which embryonic structure?

explanation.summary: Congenital preductal coarctation is thought to arise from abnormal development of the aortic arch during formation from the embryonic left fourth aortic arch, whereas postductal lesions relate to abnormal development of the descending aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: Congenital preductal coarctation is thought to arise from abnormal development of the aortic arch during formation from the embryonic left fourth aortic arch, whereas postductal lesions relate to abnormal development of the descending aorta.

questions.stem: This diagram shows dilated collateral vessels (left subclavian, internal thoracic, and intercostal arteries) rerouting blood past an aortic coarctation. As these vessels enlarge, they classically produce which radiographic sign?

explanation.summary: The enlarged intercostal arteries erode the inferior surface of the ribs as they carry collateral flow to the lower body, producing the classic rib-notching sign on chest radiograph in coarctation of the aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: The enlarged intercostal arteries erode the inferior surface of the ribs as they carry collateral flow to the lower body, producing the classic rib-notching sign on chest radiograph in coarctation of the aorta.

questions.stem: This diagram shows the layered membrane enclosing the heart. Between the two serous layers lies a potential space normally holding a small amount of fluid. What is the primary functional role of that fluid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It conducts the cardiac electrical impulse between chambers

choices.label: B
choices.text: It generates the force that drives ventricular ejection

choices.label: C
choices.text: It supplies oxygen and nutrients directly to the myocardium

choices.label: D
choices.text: It lubricates the surfaces to reduce friction as the heart contracts

choices.label: E
choices.text: It provides the main blood supply to the coronary arteries

explanation.summary: The pericardial cavity between the visceral and parietal serous layers contains a small volume of serous fluid that lubricates the surfaces, allowing frictionless movement of the beating heart. Accumulation of excess fluid here produces a pericardial effusion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pericardial cavity between the visceral and parietal serous layers contains a small volume of serous fluid that lubricates the surfaces, allowing frictionless movement of the beating heart. Accumulation of excess fluid here produces a pericardial effusion.
